**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 21</mark>**<sup>**st**</sup> **<mark>December 2009</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for September 2009** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for September world copper supply and demand in its December 2009 Copper Bulletin.  The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to the preliminary ICSG data, the apparent refined copper market balance for September showed a nominal surplus of around 3,000 metric tonnes (t).  When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, September showed a surplus of about 11,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first nine months of 2009, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of about 50,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 161,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of around 92,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of about 118,000 t) for the same period in 2008. 

In the first 9 months of 2009, world usage is estimated to have decreased by 0.8% compared with that in the same period of 2008. Although Chinese apparent usage increased by 45% this was insufficient to offset a decrease of 18.5% [1.8 million tons (Mt)] in the rest of the world.  Chinese apparent usage increased by 1.7 Mt in the first 9 months of 2009, compared with usage in the same period of 2008.<sup>*****</sup> Copper usage in the other important markets, the EU-15 countries, Japan, and the United States, decreased by 22%, 32%, and 22%, respectively. These three regions currently represent about 29% of total world copper usage. 

World mine production grew by 2.9% in the first 9 months of 2009 compared with the same period of 2008: Concentrate production grew by 1.8% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) was up by 7.4%. Indonesia, where production increased by 331,000 t (recovering from 2008 operational constraints), was the main contributor to production growth. Lower output in the two leading world producers, Chile and the United States, as well as Canada, which totalled about 180,000 t, partially offset growth in other countries. Mine production capacity utilization fell to 79.5% compared with an average rate of 80.6% in the same period of 2008. 

In the first 9 months of 2009, world refined production decreased by 0.5% compared with that in the same period of 2008: Primary production decreased by 0.5% while secondary production (from scrap) decreased by 0.1%.  Announced production cuts led to decreases in refined production of around 6% in Europe, 12.5% in North America, and 1.5% in Asia (ex-China). Increases of around 9.5% in Chile and 5.6% in China were not sufficient to offset decreases in the other regions. Refined production capacity utilization fell to 77.5% compared with an average rate of 81% in the same period of 2008. 

The average LME cash price for November 2009 was US$6,675.60 per tonne, up from the October 2009 average of US$6,287.98 per t

onne. The 2009 high and low copper prices through the end of November were US$6,945.50 and US$3,050.50 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$4,999.02 per tonne. As of the end November 2009, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 620,015 t, an increase of 230,332 t from stocks held at the end of December 2008. Compared to the October levels, stocks were up at LME and COMEX and down at SHFE.
